current_round.prompt:
From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: Goals whose candidate is already merged into the target branch loop forever in `quality` �� no supported path advances them

Body:
Bug report - Goals whose candidate is already merged into the target branch loop forever in `quality` �� no supported path advances them

  ### Refine version
  4.2.0 (linux_cli_web, native supervisor daemon, port 8082)

  ### Severity
  High �� completed, already-integrated work is permanently stuck; the queue shows 12 "in progress" goals that can never finish, and the only forward CLI verb makes it worse
  (re-queues into the same failure).

  ### Environment
  - Node: `bo2lnxnevo03-buddy`, 4-node fleet
  - Target branch: `insurity-claims` �� a SHARED integration branch that many goals build on and merge into in parallel. Because goals integrate into one shared
  branch/checkout, a later goal's `post_build` can land another goal's candidate commit into the target before that goal's Quality stage runs.

  ### Summary
  When the workflow reaches the Quality stage for a goal whose `candidate_commit` is already an ancestor of its `target_branch`, an "already-merged reconciliation" fires,
  decides Quality "could not run," and PRESERVES the goal at `quality` status. The engine then immediately re-resumes the goal from `quality`, which hits the same
  reconciliation again �� an infinite loop. Status never advances to `review`.

  ### Repro / evidence
  12 goals in this state simultaneously. For each, the activity log repeats (25+ times for a single goal):
      �� Resumed workflow from quality
      �� Already-merged reconciliation Quality could not run; target and Goal status were preserved

  Confirmed already-merged for all 12, e.g. goal 00000SZ65PBBNHVG7B24N80001:
  - base_commit=70b59a2c, candidate_commit=b217bd2c, target_branch=insurity-claims
  - `git merge-base --is-ancestor b217bd2c insurity-claims` �� true (candidate IS in target)

  `goal updated` timestamps keep bumping (so they look "active"), but status is pinned at `quality`.

  ### No supported recovery path
  - `goal retry --stage quality` �� re-queues ("Queued for Quality") and loops right back to the already-merged reconciliation (verified live on 00000SZ65PDN70RNF67WN80003).
  - `goal approve` �� rejected; requires `review` status.
  - `goal undo` �� only walks backward (done��review, cancelled��todo); cannot push quality��review.
  - No `quality��review`/promote/reconcile-resolve verb exists in `refine commands`.
  - `system doctor` reports healthy; `config quality` doesn't govern this guard.
  - Note: `system status` shows `degraded_integrations: ["operation-recovery-interrupted"]` on port 8082 �� possibly related to why the reconciliation re-fires instead of
  resolving.

  ### Expected behavior
  When the already-merged reconciliation detects that a goal's candidate is already merged into the target, it should RESOLVE the goal forward (mark it `review`, or `done`
  if Quality/Governance are otherwise satisfied) �� the work is delivered. It must NOT preserve `quality` and re-enter the resume loop.

  ### Additional asks
  1. Make the already-merged case terminal, not looping (idempotent: detect �� resolve once �� stop resuming).
  2. Provide a supported manual escape hatch for goals already stuck this way (e.g. `goal resolve-merged <id>` or allow `approve`/promote from `quality` when candidate ��
  target), so operators don't have to hand-edit durable state.
  3. Consider guarding the shared-integration-branch case: a goal's Quality stage shouldn't be invalidated just because a *sibling* goal's post_build advanced the shared
  target.

findings.description: The plan allows an unavailable reconciliation Quality run to advance solely from integration and ancestry evidence, but it does not explicitly require durable passing Quality and Governance evidence for the exact Round and candidate; delivery alone is not proof that the gates were satisfied.
findings.recommendation: Require exact-candidate passed Quality and Governance evidence before advancing to Review; otherwise terminate safely as Failed with recovery evidence.

findings.description: The plan does not require reconciliation evidence and the Quality-to-Review transition to be committed by one Goal-lock mutation fenced by the originating attempt or expected workflow revision, leaving stale-worker, manual-command, and crash windows that can preserve or overwrite Quality state.
findings.recommendation: Add one atomic resolver mutation that revalidates authority and Git observations, writes terminal evidence, and transitions status idempotently under the Goal lock.

findings.description: No checklist item verifies the loop fix, idempotent repeated/concurrent resolution, sibling advancement of local and published shared targets, unsafe failure paths, or end-to-end daemon-routed CLI and catalog behavior.

checklist.description: Consolidate automatic and operator-initiated already-merged handling into one cohesive reconciliation capability within the existing workflow and work-item service boundaries.

Keep a candidate that is merely reachable because a sibling advanced the shared target on the normal isolated Quality and Governance path, and admit reconciliation only for the authoritative current Round with its own exact integration identity.
Require durable passed Quality and Governance evidence bound to the same current Round and exact candidate commit before any already-merged resolution may advance the Goal to Review.

Revalidate under repository coordination that the exact candidate remains an ancestor of the observed local target and any required published target while allowing unrelated descendant commits and recording both observed snapshots.

Commit authority revalidation, terminal reconciliation evidence, and the Quality-to-Review transition in one idempotent Goal-lock mutation fenced by the originating Round and expected workflow revision, with repeated or concurrent callers returning the existing Review outcome.

Settle missing, mismatched, unavailable, or otherwise unsafe gate and Git evidence as Failed with durable recovery context, while retaining strict target-snapshot fencing for the existing destructive revert path after a genuine failed verdict.
Add `goal resolve-merged <id>` through the daemon API, CLI parser and dispatch, and supported command catalog so it invokes the shared resolver without weakening review-only approval semantics.

Update the affected Quality, merge-and-review, workflow consistency, and CLI intent pages to describe terminal reconciliation, exact gate requirements, shared-target ancestry, and the supported recovery action.

Add capability and workflow regression tests for loop termination, exact gate binding, idempotent repeated and concurrent settlement, sibling advancement of local and published targets, and every fail-closed or revert-fenced outcome.
Add daemon API, CLI parsing and dispatch, and command-catalog coverage proving the manual resolver reaches the shared capability and reports successful, idempotent, and rejected outcomes.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P2, P3, and P6 require exact current-Round candidate Quality and Governance passes before Review and terminate unsupported reconciliation as Failed with recovery evidence.
P5 makes authority checks, terminal evidence, and status settlement one idempotent mutation under the Goal lock, fenced by Round and workflow revision.
P9 and P10 add race, loop, shared-target, unsafe-path, daemon API, CLI, parsing, dispatch, and catalog regression coverage.

result.summary: Refine will replace the looping already-merged path with one shared, authority-fenced resolver that advances Quality to Review only when the current Round has durable passing Quality and Governance evidence for the exact candidate and confirmed integration ancestry; sibling commits may advance a shared target without invalidating isolated Quality, while missing or unsafe evidence will settle the Goal as Failed with recovery context instead of leaving it resumable, and operators will receive a daemon-routed command that invokes the same idempotent capability.

checklist.evidence: Added one FileGovernanceIntegrationService resolver used by both WorkflowQuality and the operator surface, with Goal inspection and atomic settlement owned by cohesive FileWorkItemService already_merged.rs boundaries.

Resolver admission requires the authoritative latest Round's workflow_integration identity and exact candidate match; candidate ancestry without that identity is rejected and remains on the ordinary isolated Quality path.

Resolution requires passed Quality with isolated_candidate details and exact source/current candidate plus all passed Governance states, a nonempty governance timestamp, and the newly persisted governance_candidate_commit equal to the candidate.

Under the repository Git lock, the resolver expands exact candidate and integration commits, proves candidate ancestry through the integration snapshot and current local target, fetches and proves the published target when pushed, accepts unrelated descendants, and records both observed target SHAs.

Settlement reacquires the per-Goal mutation lock, revalidates latest Round, stored WorkflowAttemptAuthority round_idx/workflow_revision, status, candidate, integration, and gate evidence, then atomically writes terminal reconciliation evidence and Review or Failed status; repeated and concurrent calls return already_resolved or already_failed.

Missing, mismatched, unsuccessful, unavailable, or non-ancestral admitted evidence settles Failed with failure_category, failure_message, timestamps, gate evidence, Git snapshots, and error context. The existing destructive revert capability and its exact target snapshot fence remain intact and tested.

Added goal resolve-merged <id> to Clap, normal daemon dispatch, /work/goals/<id>/resolve-merged handling, direct test adapter, and the supported command catalog without changing Review-only goal approve behavior.

Updated Quality, merge/review Git worktree, workflow consistency, and CLI intent pages for exact gates, shared-target descendants, terminal fail-closed settlement, idempotence, and the supported recovery command.

Added six capability tests plus a workflow regression covering loop termination, current-Round admission, exact gate and integration binding, concurrent/repeated idempotence, local and published descendant targets, missing local/published ancestry, durable Failed settlement, and revert fencing.
Added daemon action coverage for resolved, already_resolved, and rejected ancestry-only outcomes; CLI parsing and encoded daemon-route coverage; and command-catalog coverage for resolve-merged.
